Welcome to the Tracker for Windsor University School of Medicine

Your whole module in one place, so you always know what to study next.

Used by 20+ Windsor students

New here? Here's how to start

  1. Sign in with Google (it only takes a second).
  2. Pick your semester in Settings, top right of the page.
  3. Open your module, then tick things off as you study. The Planner does the rest.
  • Videos for every lecture. Pathoma, Sketchy and Bootcamp videos matched to each lecture, with the First Aid page beside it.
  • Check off what you watch. Your progress bar shows how much is left before the exam.
  • A daily study plan. It tells you what to watch each day to finish on time, and switches to the next module on its own.
  • Works on your phone and laptop. Sign in once and your checkmarks sync everywhere.
What's inside
  • Modules: MD1 (MSK101), MD3 (FBS301, NIS302, CHS303) and MD4 (RNS401, GHS402, ERS403, RMS406).
  • Videos: Pathoma, Sketchy Path, Micro and Pharm, Bootcamp, Pixorize and Dirty Medicine, matched to each lecture.
  • Book pages: First Aid and Pathoma page numbers on every row. Add your own PDFs in Settings and they open to the right page.
  • Mastery sheets: one-page reviews of the high-yield pathology for RNS401 and CHS303.
  • Planning: exam countdowns, the class schedule and a daily plan that adjusts as you check things off.

1 · Which MD year are you in?
This picks which module tabs, class schedule and overview you see. You can switch any time.
2 · 📚 Connect your PDFs
The tracker doesn't contain the textbooks (they're copyrighted) — you connect your own copy once. After that, every page badge in the tracker (📖 First Aid, 🩻 Mehlman, 💯 100 Concepts, 📄 Bootcamp notes, 🃏 Lippincott card, 📓 Pathoma) opens your PDF in a new tab right at that page.
  • How: click a PDF below → pick the file from your computer. Green dot = connected. Click again to swap it, × to remove.
  • Privacy: the file never leaves your device — this browser just remembers it. Nothing is uploaded.
  • Note: you'll need to reconnect on a different browser or device (or if you clear site data).

3 · 🦴 MSK101 Anatomy study order

Lecture order follows what the professor teaches each day (best for staying in sync with class, SGDs and labs). Bootcamp order is one flat list of videos in the order Bootcamp teaches them (best if you'd rather learn topic-by-topic at your own pace). See the pros & cons
4 · 🔄 Updates

🎬 Tutorial
A quick interactive tour of everything in the tracker: lectures, videos, First Aid pages, the planner and more. It takes about a minute.
🎞 Video source
Choose where the 🎬 video links open. Use Local folder if you have the videos saved on your computer: pick the folder once and every link plays straight from it in the tracker. Works in Chrome and Edge on a computer.
🧠 Anki button
Adds a 🧠 Anki button next to each video. One click opens Anki's card browser showing exactly that video's cards from the AnKing Step deck. Preferred: install the small Anki add-on once (keep Anki open) and the cards open straight away. Without it, the button copies the search so you can paste it into Anki's Browse screen.
⬇ Download the add-on
Install: in Anki choose Tools → Add-ons → Install from file…, pick the downloaded file, then restart Anki.
6 · 📖 How everything works
Tap a topic to expand it.
🏠 Overview tab
Shows the module you're in right now (based on today's date), this week's class schedule in colour, exam countdowns, and progress cards for the module. It's your daily starting point.
📅 Planner tab
A monthly calendar for planning your study. Days with an SGD 👥, TBL 🧩 or exam 🚨 from the class timetable are badged so you can see heavy days at a glance.
📚 Module tabs (e.g. MSK101, RNS401)
Each module has sub-tabs (e.g. Anatomy, Physiology). Each row is one lecture/topic with what to watch, how long it is, and the matching pages in your textbooks.
  • Tick the box when you finish a row — progress bars fill up, weighted by real video minutes.
  • Search box finds any topic; Show gaps only shows topics with no video; Mark all done / Clear all do bulk changes.
🔖 The little page badges (📖 🩻 💯 📄 🃏 📓)
Each badge is a shortcut to a page in one of your PDFs: 📖 First Aid, 🩻 Mehlman (high-yield notes, approved users only), 💯 100 Anatomy Concepts, 📄 Bootcamp notes, 🃏 Lippincott Microcards, 📓 Pathoma. If the PDF isn't connected yet, clicking one shows a short prompt that lets you connect it and then opens that exact page.
🎬 Bootcamp videos (MSK101)
Videos aren't linked — you watch them in your own Bootcamp account. Each row tells you exactly which one: course › chapter › video number (e.g. MSK › Ch.9 › 9.3 Clavicle Fractures) plus its length in minutes. Numbers match Bootcamp's own chapter.video numbering. Use Lecture order / Bootcamp order to pick how it's listed.
🗓️ Schedule tab & colours
The full class timetable, week by week. Each subject has its own colour strip. Special sessions stand out: 🚨 exams / quizzes / OSCEs / NBME (red), 👥 SGDs (teal), 🧩 TBLs (amber), 🔬 dissection labs (blue) and ⭐ events / orientations (dashed gold). Multi-hour sessions span their full length. The legend at the top of the tab explains every colour.
❓ Alan's Q Bank
Alan's Q Bank is a practice-question bank with detailed explanations for every answer. The explanations combine material from UWorld, Robbins and Rubin's, and other trusted sources, so you learn why each option is right or wrong, not only which one to pick. You can highlight text, flag questions and keep notes on each one. Your answers are saved in this browser.
☁️ Saving your progress
Everything you tick or type saves automatically in this browser. To keep progress across devices, use Sign in with Google (top of the page) — then it syncs to the cloud. Clearing your browser data without signing in erases local progress.
💡 Quick tips
  • New here? Do 2 · Connect PDFs first — it makes every page badge work.
  • Not sure what to study today? Open Overview → this week's schedule, then jump into your module tab.
  • If something looks out of date, use 4 · Check for updates now.

How do you want to study Anatomy?
Both use the same Bootcamp videos — they only differ in the order and layout. Pick what suits you (you can change it any time).

📅 Lecture order

Follow the professor's schedule
Pros
  • Matches what's taught each day, so you're prepped for lecture, SGD and dissection lab
  • Every row shows the date, slides and matching First Aid / Mehlman / 100 Concepts pages
  • Easy to stay on pace with the class calendar
Cons
  • Bootcamp chapters are split up and revisited across days, so you jump around
  • You may see a topic before its Bootcamp foundation video

🎬 Bootcamp order

One list, in Bootcamp's teaching order
Pros
  • Concepts build up the way Bootcamp teaches them — foundations first
  • Simple flat checklist: one tick per video, no repeats or jumping around
  • Great for going chapter by chapter at your own pace
Cons
  • Doesn't line up with the class calendar — you have to watch ahead / behind yourself
  • No day-by-day view of lectures, SGDs and labs, so it's easier to walk into one unprepared
💡 Change your mind later? Go to ⚙️ Settings → 3 · Anatomy study order (or use the "Study order" switch at the top of Anatomy). Your ticks are saved separately for each style.
How would you like to study Immunology (NIS302)?
Both options use the same Bootcamp Immunology videos and the same Ky's notes. Only the order and layout differ, and either one fully prepares you for the exam. You can switch at any time.

📅 Lecture order

Follows your class schedule
Strengths
  • Stays in step with what is taught each day, so you arrive prepared for lecture and SGD
  • Each lecture lists its Bootcamp videos, First Aid page and Ky's notes together
Worth knowing
  • Bootcamp teaches each topic by building on the one before it, so watching in lecture order can feel out of sequence and a little harder to follow at first

🎬 Bootcamp order

Follows Bootcamp's sequence
Strengths
  • Concepts build in the order the videos were designed, from lymphoid tissue through to disease
  • A single checklist with one tick per video, plus the topics only Ky's notes cover
Worth knowing
  • The sequence differs from the class calendar, so you will sometimes be ahead of or behind the lecture being taught
You can change this later using the "Study order" switch at the top of NIS302 → Microbiology. Progress is saved separately for each order.

How to use this tracker

Everything saves automatically — checkboxes, notes, planner changes (and across devices once you sign in). Quick hits below:

📚 Every module tab

  • Each module (RNS401, GHS402, ERS403, RMS406, FBS301, NIS302, CHS303) has its own Pathology / Microbiology / Pharmacology sub-tabs
  • ✅ Check a box → progress bar updates instantly, weighted by real video length
  • 🔍 Search box jumps to any topic fast
  • Show gaps only = topics with no video (need slides/First Aid instead)
  • Mark all done / Clear all for bulk changes
  • 🎬 Watch, 📖 First Aid page, 📓 Pathoma page — all pre-linked on every row. Attach your own First Aid/Pathoma PDFs once (top pills) and every page link works site-wide

📅 Planner

  • Auto-builds a day-by-day calendar from your semester start date, spacing lectures so you stay ahead by your chosen buffer
  • Per-subject countdown: time remaining, required pace, % watched
  • Drag any lecture to lock it to a day, or add a custom study session manually
  • Colored dot = subject · 🏫 = taught that day in class · red outline = behind pace · blue outline = manually scheduled

🧠 Alan's Q Bank (RNS401 sub-tab)

  • 290 questions (Robbins + Rubins), answer to see explanations for every choice
  • ✗ / ⚑ filter to wrong-only or flagged-only; ← / → arrow keys move through questions
  • Highlight, flag, or note (📝) any question — survives Reset Chapter
  • ↓ Export to Anki — every wrong/flagged/noted question, one click, ready to import

⚙️ MD3 / MD4 & Cloud save

  • Switch between MD3 and MD4 anytime from the gear icon (top right) — only that semester's tabs show up
  • Red dot next to "Cloud save" = signed out, saved to this browser only
  • Green dot = synced to your Google account
  • Sign in with Google once — checkboxes, notes, and planner then follow you to any device
⚠️ Known content gaps (no dedicated video — use the slides and First Aid):
  • Pathology: Herniations/Pseudotumor Cerebri (only partially covered by Developmental Anomalies), Neurocutaneous Disorders, Metabolic Disorders of Brain, the two "Extra Assigned Topics in RNS II" lectures.
  • Pharmacology: Local Anesthetics — Sketchy's Anesthetics & Analgesics chapter only has IV Anesthetics, Inhaled Anesthetics, and Opioids; no dedicated local anesthetics video.
  • Bonus (not tied to a specific lecture title but round out the Pathoma chapter): Nasopharynx & Larynx (Ch. 9.1–9.2), Spinal Cord Lesions (Ch. 17.2), and Meningitis (Ch. 17.3, pairs well with your MB2 Bacterial Meningitis lecture).
💬Questions, bugs, ideas? Contact the creator

Study Planner

Calendar — today through exam day

Review 🏫 = taught in class that day Red outline = behind your get-ahead buffer Blue outline = manually scheduled/dragged

Plan your own study time

Pick any video/lecture, choose a day, and optionally set your own review length in minutes. It locks into place on the calendar — drag it to move it later, or remove it from that day's detail view (click the day).

💡 This plan recalculates whenever you check a box anywhere in this file. Videos are ordered to match the actual order topics are taught in your class schedule for the current module so subjects naturally mix, and the planner tries to keep each video watched at least your buffer setting's worth of days before it's covered in class — items in red are already behind that. Drag any lecture to a different day to lock it there, or use "Plan your own study time" to schedule a specific video with a custom review length. Review days pull from whatever you've already watched, plus anything tagged as a gap topic (no dedicated video) so you don't forget to hit those with slides/First Aid.

Biochemistry — Connective Tissue, Glycolysis & Glycogen (Bootcamp + Pixorize)

Biochemistry total: ~320 min = 5h 20m (209 min Bootcamp + 90 min Pixorize + 21 min Dirty Medicine), listed in the order Dr. Shetty teaches it per the MD1 schedule (Sep 29 – Oct 21). Each row gives Dr. Shetty's slides for that session, then which Bootcamp videos to watch (chapter.video numbers match Bootcamp) and which Pixorize videos add the picture-mnemonic version. Where neither has a video for something on the slides, the row says so. The earlier biochemistry lectures (amino acids, proteins, enzymes) were in FBS100, and lipid, hemoglobin and electron-transport lectures come later in CRS102.
Two ways to learn each topic — you don't need to do both
🎬 Bootcamp — learn itThe full explanation: mechanism, why it happens and the clinical picture. Start here for every topic.
🎨 Pixorize — lock it inShort picture-mnemonic stories (click a Pixorize video and choose: watch it, or read its notes page). Best for the long or fiddly topics that won't stick after Bootcamp.
Both cover many of the same topics, so on each lecture the videos on the same topic sit next to each other. Watch Bootcamp first, then add the Pixorize video for anything you can't remember. The lecture total adds up every video listed.
Also from Dr. Shetty (module resources): 📑 MSK orientation deck 📝 Water-soluble vitamins worksheet (20 Qs — Q16–18 are vitamin C & collagen) 📝 Review key points (FBS + MSK-1 topics) 📝 Shetty Biochem Practice Q's
